finding: If every ‘L’ station were accessible, 27% of Chicagoans would live within a step-free half-mile walk of one, up from 22% today. But 64% of that gain waits on stations with no date or no money. Even then, 73% of the city lives farther away.

ledger.source: CTA - System Information - List of 'L' Stops
ledger.units: 2,746,388 residents (2020 Census) in 33,801 blocks; 144 stations + 4 under construction
method: Phases from CTA’s ASAP Strategic Plan (2024), Table 5; Racine (Blue) and Austin (Green) accessible per CTA releases
Red Line Extension stations where OpenStreetMap’s construction alignment crosses CTA’s cross streets
Half-mile step-free walk on the OpenStreetMap network (extract of 2026-11-01), as Plate III, rerun after each step
Waterlines: step-free walk to the nearest station in 2038, every eighth of a mile
caveats: 2020 population for a 2038 city; today’s sidewalks and curb ramps
Phases Three and Four and the Red–Purple stations have no date or funding; the order among them is CTA’s table order
Extension station points are approximate (main entrance street, not the entrance)
